CORRECTION, MADE THE SAME DAY AND BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS QUOTED ELSEWHERE. THE HEADLINE CONCLUSION ABOVE IS
INVERTED AND IS WITHDRAWN.
=========================================================================================================
E74 compared each feature's drug-free response against its drug response, and built its DRUG_DZ constants
by hand from E67 -- taking E67's two DRUG columns and leaving E67's NO-DRUG column behind. That column was
natural N3 sleep, and it changes the answer completely:

    feature                N3 sleep    sleep-dep    propofol       GA
    whole_head_exponent      +4.008       +0.034      +1.110   +0.937
    lempel_ziv               -2.281       -0.324      +1.551   +0.947

**whole_head_exponent responds to natural N3 sleep MORE STRONGLY THAN TO EITHER ANAESTHETIC.** It is not
pharmacology-specific and the PHARMACOLOGY label is wrong. Its silence under sleep deprivation (+0.034)
reflects the size of that manipulation -- being sleep-deprived while awake is a far smaller state change
than N3 sleep or general anaesthesia -- not a need for a drug. Its SIGN is consistent across all four
contrasts, which is the profile Challenge A wants. It is the best candidate in this comparison, not the
worst.

**lempel_ziv is the feature whose direction depends on whether a drug is involved**: negative in both
drug-free arms (-2.281 natural sleep, -0.324 deprivation) and positive in both drug arms (+1.551 propofol,
+0.947 GA). E67 flagged that reversal and could not separate it from depth; the second drug-free arm now
agrees in sign with the first, which strengthens the reversal as a fact while leaving its cause open.

BOTH DRUG-FREE ARMS AGREE IN SIGN FOR BOTH FEATURES, which is the one thing this correction adds beyond
fixing an error: the sleep-deprivation arm is a weak version of the natural-sleep arm rather than a
different phenomenon, so the two can be read together.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the primary (7 of 29 features respond against a placebo of 1.975), the G1 result
(subjective anchors move, PVT lapses do not), and the finding that Q29's calibrated ratio is unavailable on
this deposit. What is withdrawn is only the two-feature interpretation, which was the part quoted as the
result. Logged as error-catalogue rule 59.

outcome_detail:
NO TRACKING, in both arms, and it is the most consequential Challenge C result so far because the incumbents on the SAME rows track it well.

    our index, FULL (18 features)   rho = +0.0375 [-0.1501, +0.2893]   38 recordings
    our index, SAFE (11 features)   rho = +0.0417 [-0.1756, +0.1424]   39 recordings
    DOSE-I own PE31                 rho = +0.3974 [+0.3098, +0.4636] / +0.4813 [+0.4093, +0.6332]
    DOSE-I own SEF95                rho = -0.0197 [-0.1155, +0.1109] / +0.2507 [+0.0762, +0.3833]

Depth information IS present in this EEG and IS recoverable -- permutation entropy, the measure E33 named as its incumbent from Ostertag et al., reaches +0.48 on the same windows. Our index reaches +0.04.

IT IS NOT A FLAT-MODEL ARTEFACT, which the registration did not gate for and which was checked afterwards. Predictions vary on DOSE-I at sd 12.02 (FULL, 2nd-98th percentile 39.1-89.1) and 5.04 (SAFE, 30.8-50.1), against sd 5.48 on the VitalDB fit set itself. The model moves; it simply moves independently of what the clinician recorded.

M1 TRANSPORT: 11 of 18 features transport. bis_bsr and bis_quazi have INFINITE shift (near-zero IQR on one side -- burst suppression barely occurs in either cohort), bis_sfs 1.730, multiscale_entropy_slope 1.574, whole_head_exponent 1.288, lempel_ziv 1.203, exponent_high 1.122. The SAFE arm drops all seven and the answer does not change, so drift is NOT the explanation.

M2 COVERAGE differs sharply between arms and is itself informative: the FULL arm places 46.2% of windows inside [20,60) while the SAFE arm places 100.0%, because the SAFE model's whole predicted range (30.8-50.1) sits inside the licensed band. A model whose output cannot leave the band it was fitted in is not being restrained by the refusal rule; it has simply regressed to its training mean.

WHAT THIS DOES TO Q22's DELIVERABLE. Q22 licensed using the index on monitor-free deposits within [20,60) with +/-3.47 attached. That licence rested entirely on agreement with device BIS measured on the recordings it was fitted to. The first external test of whether it measures DEPTH rather than one manufacturer's OUTPUT fails. **The parsimonious reading is that the index learned to reproduce the BIS algorithm on one device and population, not anaesthetic depth** -- and reproducing a proprietary index is not the same as measuring what the index claims to measure.

THE CAVEAT THAT MUST RIDE WITH IT, and it cannot be settled with data in hand. The index was fitted to predict DEVICE BIS, and MOAA/S is a different target; if BIS itself tracked MOAA/S poorly, a BIS-faithful index would too. DOSE-I has no BIS and VitalDB has no MOAA/S, so the two references cannot be compared directly here. Published sedation studies put BIS-versus-MOAA/S correlation in the moderate-to-strong range, which makes +0.04 hard to explain that way, but this experiment does not measure it. **Either reading has the same practical consequence: the index cannot serve as a depth comparator on monitor-free deposits, which was Q22's entire purpose.**

THE MAGNITUDE IS THE RESULT AND IT DEFENDS Q35. bis_rbr's wake-versus-N3 effect is d_z = -2.743 [-3.418, -2.228] -- the largest of any feature measured on this table -- and after adjustment for real submental EMG it is still 1.440. Roughly a tenth of it is muscle. Anchors, recomputed here: exponent_high A = +0.151 [+0.028, +0.302], relative_alpha_power A = -0.307 [-0.619, -0.007].

BOTH READINGS OF THE SCALE ARE REPORTED, because A is normalised by |d0| and that flatters a large effect. RELATIVE: bis_rbr (0.102) loses less of itself to muscle than exponent_high (0.151). ABSOLUTE: bis_rbr's shrinkage |d2|-|d1| is 0.280 against exponent_high's 0.172, so it loses MORE d_z units. Both are true; the registered statistic is the relative one.

A REGISTERED PREDICTION WAS WRONG AND IT IS A FINDING. bis_bsr and bis_quazi were predicted 'identically zero in physiological sleep, because there is no burst suppression there'. They are not. bis_bsr is nonzero in 61.3 % of REM windows, 52.8 % of N1, 29.1 % of N2, 19.7 % of W and 10.6 % of N3 -- highest in the LOW-AMPLITUDE stages, which is the signature of an amplitude-threshold suppression detector false-positiving -- with one W window at BSR = 1.000, i.e. 100 % suppression in wake, which cannot be physiological. Medians are ~0 and p90s are 0.001-0.06, so the magnitudes are small, but the pattern is systematic. bis_quazi behaves the same way (nonzero in 75.4 % of REM and N1). bis_bsr's own W-vs-N3 contrast is d_z = -0.133 [-0.253, -0.098]; bis_quazi failed G2 and is reported NO-EFFECT-TO-ATTRIBUTE.

This removes one specific objection in one setting; it does not clear bis_rbr on DOSE-I, and Q35's owed registered replication is owed either way.

CHALLENGE B'S FIRST INTERPRETABLE NULL. On an unthresholded weighted graph, shortest paths are dominated by direct edges, so global efficiency is mean connectivity strength restated. Any successor testing 'network' predictors on this deposit must sparsify or threshold first, or it is re-running the same test.

THE FAMILY SURVIVOR IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A RESULT, AND THE REGISTRATION SAID SO IN ADVANCE. wpli_alpha_clustering reaches D1 rho +0.396 [+0.163, +0.591], BH q = 0.0398 over 17 features, and 0 of 400 accuracy permutations reach it. G2 FAILED AGAIN, AND THE LITERATURE CHECK AFTERWARDS SHOWS THE ANCHOR WAS THE WRONG STATISTIC. With the instrument replaced exactly as registered -- per-trial cue-locked log10(post/pre) alpha on nine sensorimotor channels, 203 runs over 30 subjects, sub-001 excluded as the smoke-test burn -- the overt anchor activemotor minus passivemotor gives d_z = +0.271 [-0.190, +0.565] over 20 subjects. THE LITERATURE CHECK THAT SHOULD HAVE RUN FIRST (rule 21). PubMed via E-utilities, records verified rather than summarised:
  * PMID 31425038 (IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng 2019), 'EEG Sensorimotor Correlates of Speed During Forearm Passive Movements': passive forearm oscillations delivered by a haptic device elicit mu and beta ERD, and the authors hypothesise and test a PROPORTIONAL relationship between SMR features and passive movement speed.
  * PMID 27529874 (IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng 2017), 'EEG Analysis During Active and Assisted Repetitive Movements': in a 2x2 of volitional intention against robotic assistance, 'statistically significant ERDs began EARLIER in conditions requiring subject's volitional contribution'.

**So passive movement produces ERD of its own, and the published volitional difference is in LATENCY.** A fixed [+0.5, +2.5] s average of alpha power cannot see a latency difference, and the anchor contrast was therefore small by construction. Both E82's and E83's failures are explained by the same thing and it is not the deposit and not the epoching -- it is the choice of summary statistic, predicted by physiology that was available before either run. ds007554 remains a good deposit for this question; the successor must use ERD ONSET LATENCY, and it must carry a stopping rule so this is not attempted indefinitely.

outcome_detail:
PREDICTS in D1 -- Challenge B's first primary to clear its own gates -- and it comes with four qualifications, all of which must travel with it.

THE RESULT. `ge_norm` (global efficiency divided by its mean over 20 weight-shuffled nulls) reaches D1 rho **+0.307 [+0.049, +0.534]** between subjects (n=62), interval excluding zero, in the direction PMID 26529439 predicted and this registration named in advance. The accuracy-permutation placebo gives [-0.235, +0.219] and the primary lies outside it. G1 (62 subjects, 123 pairs), G2 (sd 0.0451) and G3 -- the rule-60 escape check re-run on the completed table -- all passed.

QUALIFICATION 1, THE INCUMBENT. The registration required 'report the incumbent beside it, and claim superiority only on non-overlapping intervals'. **The code did not compute it**; the same defect as E73's missing P3, and it is completed here rather than dropped. `relative_alpha_power` reaches D1 rho +0.181 [-0.085, +0.415] against `ge_norm`'s +0.307 [+0.043, +0.540]. **The intervals overlap heavily, so NO superiority over the incumbent is claimed.**

QUALIFICATION 2, MULTIPLICITY. Over the five-feature family, `ge_norm`'s BH q = **0.0920** -- it does NOT survive at q = 0.05. It is the pre-declared primary, so the family correction is context rather than its bar, but a reader is entitled to both numbers and here they disagree.

QUALIFICATION 3, BETWEEN-SUBJECT ONLY. D2, the consecutive-session change design, is null: +0.120 [-0.073, +0.310] for the primary and +0.020 [-0.167, +0.202] for the incumbent. **A between-subject effect with a null within-subject change is the signature E73 refused to promote `wpli_alpha_clustering` for**, and consistency requires the same caution here -- it is what a stable trait-like confound looks like, and D1's ceiling (0.8087, E68) is lower than D2's (0.9478).

QUALIFICATION 4, ONE FAMILY MEMBER ALSO CLEARS. `iaf` -- individual alpha frequency, a genuinely different family from connectivity -- reaches D1 +0.255 [+0.018, +0.468]. Context, not a result.

WHAT IS NEW HERE AND SURVIVES ALL FOUR. E73's null was on a measure that turned out to BE mean connectivity strength (rho +0.9702 with mean degree even at 62 channels). `ge_norm` was verified to escape that family BEFORE registration (+0.2570 with mean degree) and is the only autonomous graph measure here that both escapes it and predicts. **The finding is that the escaping measure predicts where the non-escaping one did not** -- which is rule 60 paying for itself -- and not that BCI ability has been explained.

outcome_detail:
NO TRANSPORT, and it is unambiguous: **0 of 6 adult awake pairs land within +-0.5 weighted-SD units of zero. Five FAIL and one is UNDETERMINED.** Referenced to LEMON, awake eegmmidb sits at -0.963 [-1.242, -0.676] and awake ds005620 at +1.212 [+0.757, +1.647]; referenced to eegmmidb, ds005620 sits at +1.649 [+1.290, +1.990]. The awake centre moves by up to 1.6 weighted SD depending only on which cohort supplied the reference.

**The sentence 'UCE = 0 means the average awake reference population' is therefore not defensible outside the cohort the reference came from**, and every absolute threshold, alert level and cross-dataset comparison built on it inherits that displacement. This is the red-team objection stated in its own terms -- z-scoring can look stable when the raw centroids are not -- confirmed on three independent adult awake cohorts totalling 589 recordings.

G4 passed: self-referencing gives exactly 0, so the standardisation is implemented correctly and the failures are not arithmetic. G3 passed: no reference SD is near zero.

TWO WEAKNESSES, BOTH MINE, BOTH STATED RATHER THAN BURIED. (1) **THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS ABSENT.** HBN was to supply it -- children should show a LARGE offset, and a scheme showing none would not be measuring what it claims -- but HBN returned n = 0 usable recordings, because its EGI `E<n>` channel names match neither region set (QUEUE.md Q39). So the design cannot demonstrate that the scheme detects a difference it SHOULD detect, and 'it shows offsets everywhere' is not fully excluded as an alternative to 'the centroids really move'. (2) **ds004541 contributed 2 recordings instead of ~59**, because E88's cohort selector matches the substring `baseline` while that deposit's awake recordings are labelled `@start-*` and `@loc-*` -- the same rule-61 defect E92 fixed in the state parser and which E88 inherited. The six pairs reported are all between LEMON, eegmmidb and ds005620 and are unaffected; ds004541 was dropped for a bug, not a reason.

ONE DESCRIPTIVE NUMBER WORTH KEEPING: eegmmidb's frontal SD is 0.9538 against LEMON's 0.4394 and against its own posterior SD of 0.2586. G2 FAILED AND THE DIAGNOSIS IS A SUBSTANTIVE FINDING ABOUT RANK REFERENCING. The verdict is ABSENT. G1 passed (eegmmidb awake median +0.0674, inside the +-0.10 transport margin) and G4 passed (N3 negative, so the sign convention is right).

**THE PERCENTILE COORDINATE SATURATES.** The staircase requires W > N1 > N2 > N3 and returns +0.4674, -0.2837, **-0.5000, -0.5000**. N2 and N3 are both pinned at the floor -- -0.5 means BELOW THE ENTIRE LEMON AWAKE REFERENCE DISTRIBUTION, i.e. the 0th percentile. So are VitalDB's BIS [20,40) and [40,60) bands, and ds004541's anaesthetised arm. The coordinate cannot order them because they are all off the bottom of it.

**THIS QUALIFIES E91'S RECOMMENDATION MATERIALLY AND E91 COULD NOT HAVE SEEN IT.** E91 scored discrimination on a BINARY awake-versus-anaesthetised contrast, where saturation is harmless and rank won on both axes. On a GRADED depth staircase rank loses the ordering entirely. Rank referencing buys transport and pays for it in dynamic range below the reference, and the two-axis bake-off had no way to charge it that cost. For the anaesthesia use case this is decisive: a percentile-referenced index would sit pinned at 0 % through most of general anaesthesia, however well it transports.

**THE GATE PREVENTED A WRONG HEADLINE.** Had G2 not fired, P1 would have returned TWO-SIDED: DOSE-I MOAA/S 4 sits at +0.3512 [+0.1279, +0.4023], above the awake centre with an interval excluding it. But MOAA/S 4 is LIGHT SEDATION, not a hyperexcitable state. That positive placement is a cross-deposit offset -- the same displacement E88 measured -- not a Goldilocks positive arm, and it would have been reported as one.

DESCRIPTIVE AND NOT LICENSED, but each is a transport observation worth keeping: Sleep-EDFx WAKE sits at +0.4674, near the TOP of the reference, so sleep-lab awake subjects have flatter spectra than LEMON's awake adults; ds004541 sits at -0.4907 awake and -0.5000 anaesthetised, essentially its whole range below LEMON's; eegmmidb awake at +0.0674 is the only cohort that lands where the reference says awake should be. Three different awake populations, three different places on a coordinate whose zero is supposed to mean awake.

G2 FAILED AT 0.2028 AGAINST A 0.05 FLOOR, SO THE VERDICT IS ABSENT -- and the gate did exactly the job it was registered to do. It was written as 'the mechanism P1 depends on, so monotonicity without it must not be credited to the span', and monotonicity appeared while a fifth of the staircase stayed saturated.

WHAT THE SPAN REFERENCE ACTUALLY DID, and it is most of the way there. Extreme-percentile fraction on the staircase cohort fell from **0.5168 under R-AWAKE to 0.2028 under R-SPAN** -- from more than half the recordings pinned at an extreme to a fifth. The staircase went from NOT monotone (N2 and N3 tied at the floor, both -0.5023 with zero-width intervals) to **monotone**: W +0.3073, N1 -0.2025, N2 -0.5279, N3 -0.5838. And transport did NOT degrade -- awake eegmmidb sits at +0.0419 under R-SPAN against +0.0651 under R-AWAKE, both inside the +-0.10 margin. **Had G2 not gated, both co-primaries would have passed.** G1 confirmed zero shared subject ids between the references and the test cohorts.

WHY IT IS STILL SHORT, and the diagnosis is specific. **N3's interval is zero-width at -0.5838: every single N3 recording is at the floor of the extended reference.** N2 separated from N3 only because N2 is partly inside the reference's support. The suppressed anchor is ds005620's propofol SEDATION, which does not reach the depth of N3 sleep, so the reference gained support -- but not enough of it, and not in the region that matters most.

SO RULE 62 SURVIVES AND SHARPENS: it is not enough for the reference to span 'awake to suppressed'. **It must reach as deep as the deepest state to be measured**, and a sedation cohort cannot anchor a scale that has to resolve deep NREM or surgical anaesthesia. THREE REFERENCES, EACH ADDING SUPPORT, EVERY NUMBER MOVING THE RIGHT WAY:
   R_AWAKE      n=215   extreme fraction 0.5168   staircase NOT monotone   transport +0.0651

A gate whose threshold is a round number measures the round number.

outcome_detail:
THE REGISTERED VERDICT IS (c) AND I AM WITHDRAWING IT, because the criterion it cleared was satisfied VACUOUSLY and I wrote the criterion.

WHAT RAN. All four gates passed -- G1 the hybrid equals rank to 1e-9 inside the reference IQR, G2 259 distinct inputs above the reference maximum received 259 distinct scores, G3 zero shared subject ids, G4 direction. S8 satisfied C1 (staircase monotone, N3 interval non-degenerate) and C2 (transport +0.0651, exactly equal to rank's, since the tail never touches the bulk where awake eegmmidb lives).

**WHY IT IS WITHDRAWN: N3's interval under the hybrid is 0.000002 wide.** N2's is 0.000386. Against E95's span-deep reference on the same data, N3 is 0.007614 and N2 0.025381 -- **three to four orders of magnitude more resolution.** The exponential tail decays so fast that every N3 recording compresses into a two-parts-per-million band. The ordering exists; the scale does not. C1 was written as 'non-degenerate (width > 0)' precisely to avoid a round-number threshold after rule 63 was earned twice today -- **and a structural criterion turned out to be satisfiable by a hair, which is the same failure wearing different clothes.** A criterion must be able to distinguish a real effect from its own resolution whether it is a threshold or a structural property.

THE SUBSTANTIVE ANSWER, WHICH THE EXPERIMENT DID PRODUCE. **The span reference DOMINATES the tail model on both axes.** Span-deep: N3 resolution 0.0076, transport +0.0381. Hybrid: N3 resolution 0.000002, transport +0.0651. Reworking the FLOOR beats reworking the SCALING, and it is not close. That answers the question this experiment was commissioned to answer, in the opposite direction from its prediction.

A THIRD DEFECT, IN C2 ITSELF. S1_z's transport is reported as +0.2177 against rank's +0.0651, and **those are not on the same scale** -- one is in standard deviations, the other in percentile units. The S8-versus-S3 comparison is valid because both are percentiles of the same reference; the comparison against z is not, and no conclusion may be drawn from it. z's genuine property, visible in its stage medians (W +2.18 to N3 -4.69, N3 interval 0.488 wide), is that it has real dynamic range -- which was never in doubt and is not what E88 refuted.

WHAT SURVIVES: the hybrid is a correct implementation of a sound idea that buys almost nothing here, because an exponential tail fitted to an awake reference's decile is far too light for a distribution whose suppressed states sit at 2.7 against a reference maximum of 2.0. A heavier-tailed model (a GPD with a fitted positive shape rather than shape 0) might do better and was not tried; but the span reference already achieves what it would be trying to achieve, using data instead of extrapolation, and 'unverifiable exactly where it is used' is a permanent property of any tail model.

**CONSEQUENCE FOR E86: qualification 3 dissolves.** A measure that is stable within a person cannot produce a positive change-score correlation, so D2's null (+0.120 [-0.073, +0.310]) is expected by construction rather than evidence against D1. E86's other three qualifications -- overlapping intervals with the incumbent, BH q = 0.0920, and `iaf` also clearing -- are untouched.

**THE RECIPROCAL OBLIGATION, WRITTEN INTO THE REGISTRATION, FIRES.** E73 refused to promote `wpli_alpha_clustering` for three reasons, the third being a sign reversal in D2. For a trait-like measure a change score is noise and noise takes either sign, so **that third reason is not valid** and E73's refusal now rests on two: it was not pre-declared, and a measure that wins only in the family scan has not won. The refusal stands; one of its legs does not.

**THE FINDING NOBODY ASKED FOR, AND IT IS A REAL COST OF RULE 60's REMEDY.** The raw graph measures are far more reliable than the normalised one: `ge` +0.7830, `deg` +0.7847, `alpha_prom` +0.8411 against `ge_norm`'s +0.4288. Dividing by a weight-shuffled null removes the between-subject strength component -- which is exactly the most reliable part of the signal -- so the measure that escapes mean connectivity (rule 60's requirement) pays for it in test-retest reliability. **Escaping a confounded family and being reliable are in tension, and this is the first time this project has measured that price.**

DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, and post-hoc: at ICC 0.429 for the feature and E68's 0.8087 for stable-ability accuracy, E86's observed +0.307 disattenuates to roughly +0.58. That is an attenuation correction, not a measurement, and it is quoted so a reader can see the scale of the reliability cost -- not as a result.

SCOPE: reliability is not validity. A perfectly reliable measure can be reliably irrelevant, and this decides only how D2's null should be read.
placebo: the two controls ARE the placebo structure: a measure known to be reliable and a per-session random draw, both through the identical estimator on the identical sessions
primary: ICC(2,1) of ge_norm across sessions within subject, subject bootstrap; the verdict is whether it lies closer to the TRAIT control (iaf) or the NOISE control (per-session Gaussian) -- a comparison, not a threshold (rule 63); NOT-COMPUTABLE branch named first
question: Is ge_norm a TRAIT or a STATE? If trait-like, E86's null within-subject change design is expected by construction and its qualification dissolves; if state-like, the null is evidence against the between-subject result.

deposit: VitalDB vitaldb_grid.csv, 250 cases; 92 contribute a (case, BIS band) cell, 106 cells
gates: G1 >= 40 cases and >= 60 cells
G2 bracket: the timestamp control must be DIRECTION-DEPENDENT by construction and a per-window Gaussian must not be
G3 both sides of every cell come from the same BIS band, asserted not assumed
instrument_changed: the state label moves from a clinician's MOAA/S to the monitor's BIS, which changes the estimand to the EEG component BIS does not capture; the docstring states this rather than eliding it
outcome_detail:
NO FEATURE IS DIRECTION-DEPENDENT. Seven are DIRECTION-INVARIANT at +-0.25 within-case SD (emg_beta_gamma_fraction, emg_kurtosis, exponent_gamma, relative_alpha_power, relative_delta_power, spectral_edge_95, spectral_entropy); eleven are UNDETERMINED. 94 cases, 110 (case, BIS band) cells. Both machinery controls bracketed correctly -- the timestamp at -1.413 [-1.469, -1.359] and a per-window Gaussian at -0.058 [-0.182, +0.063].

**THE PLACEBO FIRED SEVEN TIMES AND THAT IS THE RESULT.** Seven features returned a gap whose interval excluded zero -- critical_slowing_ar1 -0.125 [-0.191, -0.065], exponent_high -0.166 [-0.267, -0.064], exponent_low -0.097, lempel_ziv -0.117, multiscale_entropy_slope -0.149, pac_slow_alpha +0.126 and **whole_head_exponent -0.159 [-0.247, -0.069]** -- and EVERY ONE lay inside the random-split placebo distribution. Without the placebo this experiment would have reported seven direction-dependent features including the aperiodic exponent itself.

WHY, AND IT GENERALISES. The BIS minimum sits near the middle of a case, so 'before vs after the minimum' is very nearly 'first half vs second half'. **Any feature with a within-case time trend produces a gap, and the trend has nothing to do with hysteresis.** The random-split placebo preserves the group sizes and the band structure and destroys only the direction of travel, so it isolates exactly that. Now rule 64.

**THIS IS A WARNING FOR E80**, which is registered and unrun on DOSE-I with the same split-at-the-extremum structure. E80 carries the same random-split placebo, so it will catch the same artefact -- but its results must be read placebo-first, and a direction-dependent feature there means nothing until it clears that comparison.

THREE FEATURES WERE NOT COMPUTABLE (n=0): uce_v1, wpli_alpha and spatial_participation_ratio, all empty on VitalDB because it is a single-channel deposit. Consistent with Q39 and reported rather than silently dropped.

SCOPE, restated because it is the sentence most likely to be lost: at matched BIS these are statements about the component of the EEG that BIS does NOT capture, since BIS is computed from the same signal. They are not statements about drug versus state. And DIRECTION-INVARIANT is a necessary condition passed, never a sufficient one.
placebo: each case re-split at a RANDOM index preserving group sizes, BIS band structure intact, 200 draws; destroys direction of travel and nothing else
primary: per feature, standardised descent-minus-emergence gap at matched 10-point BIS band, case-level bootstrap; EQUIVALENCE at +-0.25 within-case SD for DIRECTION-INVARIANT, interval excluding 0 for DIRECTION-DEPENDENT, UNDETERMINED named as its own outcome
question: At MATCHED BIS, does the aperiodic exponent depend on direction of travel through the anaesthetic? Equivalently: does the component of the EEG that BIS does not capture carry hysteresis information?

deposit: VitalDB vitaldb_grid.csv, 5,798 windows with SR+BIS+exponent, 977 positive (16.9 %), 140 of 247 cases
gates: G1 the incumbent must be alive out of bag, else the result is about the label (the E61 trap)
G2 >= 100 cases and >= 300 positive windows
G3 a Gaussian negative control must not ADD
instrument_changed: the endpoint moves from emergence proximity, where BIS is missing in 70 % of windows, to device-measured suppression, where it is not
outcome_detail:
HURTS -- the registered wrong-direction branch, and it fired. Adding the aperiodic exponent to a BIS-only model makes out-of-bag detection of device-measured suppression **WORSE**: increment **-0.0306 [-0.0524, -0.0101]** over 5,798 windows, 247 cases, 977 positive (16.9 %). That is not a null and must not be reported as one: the exponent is variance the model spends capacity on and does not generalise across cases.

THE INCUMBENT WAS ALIVE AND THERE WAS ROOM. BIS alone reaches out-of-bag AUC **0.7848** -- strong, as expected since BIS incorporates a burst-suppression subparameter, but nowhere near a ceiling, so this is not a headroom artefact. G2 and G3 passed; the Gaussian negative control returned NO INCREMENT (-0.0022 [-0.0115, +0.0003]), so the machinery is not simply penalising any extra column.

**THE MUSCLE ARM LOCATES THE MECHANISM.** With the monitor's own EMG channel already in the baseline, the exponent neither helps nor hurts: -0.0027 [-0.0132, +0.0008], NO INCREMENT. **The harm in A1 disappears once EMG is controlled**, which says the exponent is injecting muscle-related variance that misleads a suppression model. That is exactly what E43 measured from the other direction -- at matched state a broadband slope fitted through 20-45 Hz is MORE muscle-associated than BIS, because BIS carries explicit EMG suppression and an aperiodic fit does not.

The artefact-band arm (BIS < 60, SQI >= 50) is unchanged in direction and slightly worse: -0.0379 [-0.0633, -0.0127]. It is secondary because it selects rows on the incumbent (rule 49).

CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY FOR THE PRODUCT FRAMING: **on this deposit a single-channel aperiodic exponent should not be added to BIS for suppression detection.** E90 showed the self-computed index is AVAILABLE where the vendor's is not; E99 shows that where both are available, adding it to BIS costs accuracy on the deep-side failure mode. Availability and usefulness are separate questions and the two results answer them differently.

LIMITS. VitalDB is single-channel, so this is a UCE-F-like measure at best (Q39). The model is a regularised linear one; a different model class might use the exponent differently, and this result does not exclude that. And the label is the device's own suppression ratio, not an independent scoring of the raw EEG.
placebo: A3 MUSCLE -- the monitor's own EMG channel added to the baseline, not a gamma or scalp proxy
primary: out-of-bag AUC increment of BIS + whole_head_exponent over BIS alone for meta_sr > 0, clustered on CASE, 400 replicates, UNRESTRICTED (rule 49); HURTS branch named first
question: Does the aperiodic exponent add to BIS for detecting device-measured burst suppression -- against an incumbent that partly computes suppression as one of its own subparameters?

deposit: Sleep-EDFx five-stage windows, per-channel Fpz-Cz and Pz-Oz, 142 subjects; SC4001E0 excluded as smoke-test burn
gates: G1 >= 50 subjects with all five stages in both tables
G2 non-degenerate W-to-N3 axis per subject per measure; failures dropped and counted
G3 known effect: delta must increase W->N3 in more subjects than a Gaussian control (rule 63 -- a comparison, not a fixed fraction)
G4 muscle: submental EMG's own axis position reported, and P1 recomputed after residualising on it; a P1 that survives only before adjustment is muscle and the verdict says so
instrument_changed: the spatial reduction: whole-head median -> the two derivations kept separate, which is the one thing E93's coordinate could not express
outcome_detail:
**THE MEASURE IS NOT THE PROBLEM.** The improvement is real, tiny, not posterior-specific, and entirely muscle. E95's reading -- that the coordinate tracks arousal rather than experience -- survives the best available challenge to it, which strengthens it.

P1 cleared its interval: position(posterior 1-4 Hz) - position(whole-head exponent) = d_z **-0.257 [-0.367, -0.159]**, so posterior delta does place REM closer to wake. **But the median shift is -0.052 on a 0-to-1 axis** -- REM moves from 0.479 to 0.440, which is not a stage crossing, it is a nudge.

**G4 KILLS IT. After residualising every measure on submental EMG within subject, P1 is d_z -0.000 [-0.134, +0.245].** The effect vanishes exactly. And the reason is visible in the EMG's own placement: submental muscle sits at REM position **+1.094**, i.e. BEYOND the N3 end of the axis -- REM has less muscle than deep sleep. Textbook atonia, independently confirming E70's finding on a different measure and a different statistic.

**P2 FOUND NO POSTERIOR SPECIFICITY**: posterior minus frontal d_z +0.011 [-0.118, +0.367]. The locality that motivated the whole design is absent, so even the nudge is about low-frequency power generally rather than about posterior cortex. (The frontal position statistic is also unstable -- IQR [-1.355, +0.293] -- because it is a ratio and frontal delta's W-to-N3 span is small or reversed in some subjects. Posterior is well behaved at IQR [+0.255, +0.556]. A ratio-based position statistic needs a non-degenerate denominator and G2 only excluded exact zeros.)

G3 passed decisively: delta increases from W to N3 in 92.1 % of subjects frontally and 97.9 % posteriorly, against a 52.9 % Gaussian control. The machinery reproduces the textbook effect, so the null is not about broken staging or a broken spectral estimate.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS.** It does NOT refute Siclari et al. (PMID 28394322). They used high-density EEG with serial awakenings and dream reports, contrasting the PRESENCE and ABSENCE of experience within stage; we have two bipolar derivations, no dream reports, and a between-stage contrast. This shows their remedy does not transfer to what this deposit can measure -- not that their result is wrong. A proper test needs dream reports, and no deposit this project can reach has them.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FRAMING: three independent routes now place REM with sleep rather than wake on this project's measures -- E69's fraction-nearer-wake, E95's axis position, and E100's per-channel low-frequency version -- and in two of the three the placement has been measured to be substantially muscle. **The coordinate should be described as an arousal axis.**
placebo: the frontal channel IS the specificity control -- Siclari's claim is posterior, so a frontal effect of equal size refutes the locality that motivated the design
primary: P1 position(posterior 1-4 Hz relative power) - position(whole-head exponent) on each subject's own W-to-N3 axis, paired d_z; PREDICTED NEGATIVE; REVERSED branch named first. P2 locality: posterior minus frontal, predicted negative -- if frontal matches, there is no locality
question: Does a POSTERIOR low-frequency measure place REM closer to wake than the whole-head aperiodic coordinate does -- i.e. is the spatial reduction what loses REM, rather than the claim being wrong?

deposit: ds005620 acq-tms, 55 recordings, 53 ok / 2 too_few_pulses; 64 ch at 5 kHz, task-awake and task-sed WITHIN subject. Pulses detected from the SIGNAL, never from a marker file, because both shipped marker formats are temporally wrong (rule 65). sub-1016 and sub-1074 excluded as burn-in (rule 26), leaving 14 subjects with both conditions.
gates: G1 >= 12 subjects with both conditions
G2 a perturbation was actually measured: real_evoked_rms > sham_evoked_rms, interval excluding 0; failure gives ABSENT, not negative (rule 31)
G3 DETECTION PARITY on n_pulses, iti_median and det_separation -- any difference downgrades to CONFOUNDED-BY-DETECTION regardless of the primary (rule 32)
G4 positive control: spont_exponent must itself separate the states, vs a Gaussian on the same pairs (rule 63)
G5 non-degenerate regressor -- residualising on a constant is vacuous (E96's C1 failure)
instrument_changed: E92 asked whether two REGIONS of the spontaneous signal decouple and found they do not. E103 changes the instrument to a PERTURBATION -- an externally imposed input with a sham arm cut from the same recording -- which is the one thing a spontaneous measure cannot be made into by re-deriving it.
outcome_detail:
ABSENT AT G4 -- the positive control failed and the design refused to emit a verdict (rule 31). spont_exponent separated awake from sedated at d_z -0.4765 (RIGHT direction: sedated higher) against a Gaussian 95th of 0.5982 over 14 subjects, so it did not clear.

G1, G2, G3 and G5 all PASSED, and G2 is worth recording because it was the gate the feasibility note demanded: **a perturbational response WAS measured**, real-minus-sham evoked RMS +4.1139 [+0.0910, +9.4649]. Detection parity held on all three statistics -- n_pulses +0.4762 [-0.1667, +1.2143], iti_median -0.0012 [-0.0356, +0.0327], det_separation +103.98 [-411.42, +629.40] -- so the arms were not being detected differently. Extraction drop-out was balanced: too_few_pulses 1 of 17 awake and 1 of 38 sed (rule 14).

THE CAUSE IS A BUG IN THE EXTRACTOR, NOT THE DEPOSIT, and the diagnostic is independent of the primary. On the SAME deposit and the SAME subjects, the existing non-TMS extraction separates the states at d_z -0.9909 over 20 subjects against a Gaussian 95th of 0.4858 -- it CLEARS comfortably. What differs is how the exponent was computed: the perturbation extractor concatenated ~46 pre-pulse segments of 0.4 s each and then ran Welch with a 1.0 s window, so **every window straddled ~2.5 segment boundaries**. That is rule 27 -- a mask that compresses out bad samples glues time together -- and it corrupts a spectral slope whatever the result would have been. The bug is identifiable without reference to the outcome; the positive control is what made anyone look, which is what positive controls are for.

The verdict stands as ABSENT. E104 is the successor with the spectral estimate fixed; the primary, the cohort, the gates, the thresholds and the placebos are unchanged.
placebo: PRIMARY PLACEBO: awake/sed labels flipped at random within subject, 500 draws -- the exact permutation null for a two-condition paired design; real d_z inside its central 95 % is WITHDRAWN. SECOND PLACEBO, the one that matters most: the identical analysis on sham_evoked_lz ALONE. If the sham matches the primary, what separates the states is the complexity of ongoing EEG and 'perturbational' is decoration.
primary: paired d_z, awake minus sedated, of the residual of (real_evoked_lz - sham_evoked_lz) after regressing out spont_exponent measured on the same bytes. DECOUPLING, not increment. INVERTED (sedated higher) named first. PREDICTED: a second axis is detected, at ~40 %.
question: IS THERE A SECOND AXIS? Does a perturbational (TMS-evoked) response carry state information beyond the spontaneous aperiodic exponent -- the discovery-shaped version of Challenge A, asked because every measure this project has taken so far reduces to one arousal axis.
